title: DotHash: Estimating Set Similarity Metrics for Link Prediction and Document Deduplication

problem.claim: Exact set-similarity computation across all pairs can become intractable as the amount of data increases.

gap.claim: Existing popular estimators such as MinHash and SimHash do not provide an estimator for the Adamic-Adar index or the related metric family described by the authors.

contributions.claim: DotHash is an unbiased estimator for the intersection size of two sets.
DotHash can estimate the Jaccard index, the Adamic-Adar index, and a related family of set-similarity metrics.
The authors formally define the related metric family and provide theoretical bounds on estimate-error probabilities.

stated_novelty.claim: To the authors' knowledge, DotHash is the first method that can estimate the Adamic-Adar index and a related family of metrics.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that DotHash is more accurate than other estimators for link prediction and duplicate-document detection, with the same complexity and similar comparison time.
The authors report analyzing DotHash's empirical performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Set-similarity metrics support data-mining tasks including Web-search deduplication and social-network link prediction.
Exact pairwise similarity computation can be intractable at increasing data scales, motivating efficient estimators.
MinHash and SimHash are popular estimators used in large-scale applications, but advancing estimators remains important.
DotHash estimates set intersections and extends estimation to the Jaccard index, Adamic-Adar index, and related metrics, with theoretical error bounds.
The authors report greater accuracy than other estimators in link prediction and duplicate-document detection at the same complexity and similar comparison time.

source_observation.claim: A set-intersection estimator can be used to estimate multiple set-similarity metrics, including Jaccard and Adamic-Adar.

interpretation.claim: A reusable estimator for a primitive quantity may support several downstream metrics.

application.claim: When designing scalable similarity systems, consider estimating a shared primitive that can serve multiple task-specific metrics.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this approach is preferable for metrics beyond the reported family or workloads.

source_observation.claim: The authors report higher accuracy than other estimators while retaining the same complexity and similar comparison time.

interpretation.claim: Estimator quality should be evaluated jointly with computational cost and comparison time.

application.claim: Benchmark scalable estimators using accuracy together with complexity and runtime-related measures.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide the experimental settings, datasets, error magnitudes, or statistical support for this comparison.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify DotHash's algorithmic construction or estimator formula.
The abstract does not provide the exact theoretical bounds or assumptions.
The abstract does not identify datasets, baselines, experimental protocols, or quantitative accuracy results.
